findings.issue_text: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on the item's datetime attribute instead of converting to a timestamp first, so build_cursor raises TypeError on any non-empty page for the audit-log endpoint ordered by -datetime

OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value without ms-to-datetime conversion, so build_queryset applies an integer as datetime__gte/__lte and any non-zero cursor fails or filters incorrectly

In organization_auditlogs.py, enable_advanced is computed unconditionally before checking use_optimized, and organization_context.member is None for org-token, integration-token, and non-member superuser requests, causing AttributeError 500s even without the optimized_pagination parameter

OptimizedCursorPaginator's 'advanced' branch passes a negative start_offset (and possibly negative stop) to a Django QuerySet slice, which raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.'), producing user-triggerable unhandled 500s; the comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is false

BasePaginator.get_result clamps a negative offset to 0 only when is_prev is false; with is_prev set the negative offset is passed to the queryset slice and raises Django ValueError, so negative offsets should be validated (400) or clamped in both paths

The enable_advanced gate treats member.has_global_access as 'authorized administrator', but global access is granted to every member in open-membership orgs and any member with an all-teams role; a privileged branch should check a scope or role instead

Comments in OptimizedCursorPaginator claim negative offsets enable access beyond pagination bounds and are safe due to queryset-level permission checks; neither is true (Django rejects negative slices and no such permission check exists), misleading future maintainers
Comment in BasePaginator saying 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' for negative offsets is incorrect since it raises; the comment should be removed or corrected

The new public optimized_pagination=true query parameter on a documented endpoint is not added to API docs, the parameter schema, or the @extend_schema declaration, and it silently changes cursor format semantics

No tests were added for OptimizedCursorPaginator, the negative-offset handling in BasePaginator, or the new endpoint branch; a basic pagination test with the optimized flag would have caught the datetime/cursor bugs

OptimizedCursorPaginator performs the identical offset-slice query as BasePaginator with no index, keyset, or count optimization, so the performance claims in the PR title and docstring are unsupported

goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BasePaginator.get_result clamps a negative offset to 0 only when is_prev is false; with is_prev set the negative offset is passed to the queryset slice and raises Django ValueError, so negative offsets should be validated (400) or clamped in both paths

adjudication.rationale: In `BasePaginator.get_result`, the new logic sets `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. This means if a client provides a cursor with `is_prev=true` and a negative `offset`, `start_offset` will be negative and the code will execute `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and will raise an exception (typically `AssertionError`/`ValueError`), causing a 500 instead of a controlled behavior (clamp or 400). The diff also explicitly starts allowing negative offsets in `Cursor` (comment) without validation, making this scenario plausible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The enable_advanced gate treats member.has_global_access as 'authorized administrator', but global access is granted to every member in open-membership orgs and any member with an all-teams role; a privileged branch should check a scope or role instead

adjudication.rationale: In the new audit log endpoint logic, the privileged path is explicitly described as being for “authorized administrators”, but the actual gate is `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. `has_global_access` is not an administrator-specific check; it denotes broad org/project access and can apply to non-admin roles/members. As a result, the new `optimized_pagination` path (including `enable_advanced_features=True`) can be enabled by users who are not necessarily “administrators”, which is inconsistent with the intent expressed in the diff and is a concrete authorization/gating defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Comments in OptimizedCursorPaginator claim negative offsets enable access beyond pagination bounds and are safe due to queryset-level permission checks; neither is true (Django rejects negative slices and no such permission check exists), misleading future maintainers

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` explicitly allows `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, and then slices the queryset as `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django `QuerySet` slicing does not support negative indices (it raises an error rather than “handling boundary conditions automatically”), so both the comment and the code path are misleading/incorrect and can introduce a runtime failure if a negative offset cursor is ever provided. Additionally, within this diff there is no “permissions checked at the queryset level” logic in the paginator; it simply operates on whatever queryset it is given, so the comment’s safety claim is not substantiated by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Comment in BasePaginator saying 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' for negative offsets is incorrect since it raises; the comment should be removed or corrected

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a comment in `BasePaginator.get_result` claiming negative offsets are "safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions", while the code path for `cursor.is_prev` still allows `start_offset = offset` (potentially negative) and slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. In Django, `QuerySet` slicing with a negative start/stop raises (negative indexing is not supported), so the comment is factually incorrect and could mislead reviewers/maintainers about runtime behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new public optimized_pagination=true query parameter on a documented endpoint is not added to API docs, the parameter schema, or the @extend_schema declaration, and it silently changes cursor format semantics

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new optional query parameter (`optimized_pagination=true`) that changes which paginator is used, but the claim that this is a “documented endpoint” and that the parameter is missing from “API docs, the parameter schema, or the @extend_schema declaration” is not verifiable from the provided diff (no documentation or schema annotations are shown/modified here). The statement that it “silently changes cursor format semantics” is also not directly demonstrated in the diff (we can see a different paginator and potential negative offsets, but no explicit cursor format/encoding contract is shown here to prove a semantic break).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests were added for OptimizedCursorPaginator, the negative-offset handling in BasePaginator, or the new endpoint branch; a basic pagination test with the optimized flag would have caught the datetime/cursor bugs

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new paginator class and changes slicing logic, but the proposed finding is primarily a process complaint (“no tests were added”) and goes further to claim tests “would have caught the datetime/cursor bugs,” which is speculative and not demonstrated by the diff itself. While it’s true no test files are shown in this diff, lack of tests is not, by itself, a verifiable functional defect introduced by the code change, and the assertion about specific bugs is not grounded in the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OptimizedCursorPaginator performs the identical offset-slice query as BasePaginator with no index, keyset, or count optimization, so the performance claims in the PR title and docstring are unsupported

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` ultimately does the same `queryset[start_offset:stop]` slicing pattern as the existing paginator for the normal (non-negative) case, but it also adds a distinct branch that allows negative offsets when `enable_advanced_features` is set. The proposed finding is primarily an argument that the PR’s *performance claims* are unsupported rather than identifying a concrete bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff. Also, whether there is “no keyset optimization” cannot be verified from this diff because `build_queryset(...)` (which is where keyset-style filtering would occur) is inherited and not shown here. So this is not a strictly verifiable problem in the changed code itself.
